title: The symmetric algebra of a finitely presented module is a finitely presented algebra, generated by generators of the module
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-module, with symmetric algebra $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\operatorname{Sym}^n_R(M)$ and its canonical $R$-linear map $\iota_M:M\to\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property] (the inclusion $M=\operatorname{Sym}^1_R(M)\subseteq\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$). (a) If $m_1,\dots,m_n$ generate $M$ as an $R$-module, then $\iota_M(m_1),\dots,\iota_M(m_n)$ generate $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ as an $R$-algebra. (b) If $M$ is a finitely presented $R$-module (there is an exact sequence $R^{\oplus m}\to R^{\oplus n}\to M\to0$, Stacks, Algebra, Definition 0518), then $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra (isomorphic to $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(g_1,\dots,g_m)$ with $g_1,\dots,g_m$ linear forms); and then for every finitely generated ideal $\mathfrak a\subseteq\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ the quotient $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)/\mathfrak a$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra.

proof.text: Prove the algebra-generator assertion by SymmetricAlgebra.induction. For the canonical images, use Submodule.span_induction on the given spanning family; linearity and closure under scalar multiplication, addition, and multiplication give membership in the generated subalgebra. This is the generation form of the universal property.

Use Module.FinitePresentation.exists_fin' to obtain a surjective linear map p : (Fin n -> R) -> M. Its kernel is finitely generated by Module.FinitePresentation.fg_ker. Choose a finite generating family y using Submodule.fg_iff_exists_fin_generating_family. The symmetric-algebra quotient theorem gives surjectivity of the constructed lift phi and identifies its kernel with Ideal.span (iota '' ker p). Span induction shows this ideal is generated by the finite family iota(y j).

For the standard basis b of Fin n -> R, set e := SymmetricAlgebra.equivMvPolynomial b and f := phi composed with e.symm. Transport the kernel ideal along e using Ideal.map_span, Ideal.map_comap_of_equiv and RingHom.comap_ker. Construct Algebra.Generators.ofSurjective for the images f(X i) and an Algebra.Presentation with relations e(iota(y j)). Expanding y j by b.sum_repr proves each relation is the linear form sum_i (b.repr (y j) i) * X i. Algebra.Presentation.finitePresentation_of_isFinite gives the algebra finite-presentation assertion.
Install the proved finite-presentation proposition locally and apply Algebra.FinitePresentation.quotient to every finitely generated ideal.
